title: The asteroid thread
text:
The asteroid thread

What we know so far

The story gives **8,500 m/s** at **15°** from the axis toward Earth. What does "at **15°**" mean?

Today

Velocity has COMPONENTS: parts along two axes. One points toward Earth. The other is at a right angle to it. We need both to **predict the path**.

title: A velocity vector has two components
text:

Target R2 Draw

A velocity vector has two components

For motion on a flat surface, choose x and y axes at right angles.

A velocity of **+4 m/s** east and **+3 m/s** north is one slanted motion. Both parts happen at once.

|v| = √(**4²** + **3²**) = **5 m/s**

title: One motion, two components
text:
**2026**-XJ · The Other Direction · Graphic novel, page **15**

One motion, two components

In the made-up story, velocity is 8,500 meters each second at fifteen degrees from the toward-Earth axis. It has two parts at right angles: about 8,210 meters each second toward Earth and 2,200 meters each second sideways.

These two parts lie at right angles. Together, they describe one velocity at one time.

Why do **8,210** and **2,200** not add to **8,500** as ordinary numbers?

A smaller component still matters

The math uses steady velocity for 1.6 times ten to the seventh seconds. It gives about 131 million kilometers toward Earth and 35 million sideways. Mr. Antocci says this is a simple model. It is not a full orbit prediction.

Over six months, even the smaller sideways rate leads to a large change in position.

**What else** do you need to know to **find the final position**?
